title: EKS 1.36 cluster is scheduled to leave standard support
summary: The Amazon EKS release calendar gives 1.36 end of standard support on 2027-08-02 and end of extended support on 2028-08-02. A cluster past end of standard support is billed at the extended-support rate for every hour it stays on 1.36.

sources.title: Amazon EKS: Understand the Kubernetes version lifecycle

constraints: Amazon EKS upgrades one minor version at a time, so cross each intervening minor version and read its upgrade notes before applying the next one.
A control plane and its node groups upgrade separately: raise the control plane first, then every node group and every add-on that pins a Kubernetes version.
Managed node groups and self-managed nodes do not follow a control-plane upgrade, so a node group left behind keeps running the older release line.

steps.title: Raise the control-plane version
steps.instructions: Run aws eks update-cluster-version with the version in the replacement, or set version and spec.version in the CloudFormation, Terraform, or eksctl declaration of the cluster, and confirm the result with aws eks describe-cluster.

steps.title: Raise the node groups
steps.instructions: Run aws eks update-nodegroup-version for each managed node group, and replace the Amazon EKS optimized AMI in the launch template of each self-managed group so its nodes roll onto the new version.

steps.title: Update the add-ons that pin a version
steps.instructions: Set kube-proxy, Amazon VPC CNI, and CoreDNS to the version Amazon EKS recommends for the new cluster version, and check any other add-on that declares a Kubernetes version.

steps.title: Remove APIs the new version deleted
steps.instructions: Read the Kubernetes deprecation guide for every minor version crossed and replace removed API versions in manifests and Helm charts before applying.

verification.purpose: Confirm the API server reports the new version.
Confirm every node runs a kubelet of the new version.
Confirm the manifests still validate against the new API versions.
